pr_body:
##### Summary
Fixes #8731 

##### Component Name
Collector
##### Test Plan
The socket was not merged on `kernel-collector` repository yet, so it is necessary to do an additional step before to test this PR.

1 - Install netdata and do not star it : `./netdata-installer.sh --dont-start-it`
2 - Get the file:
[files_updated.zip](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/files/4683782/files_updated.zip)


3 - Extract everything inside `/usr/libexec/netdata/plugins.d/`
4 - Run Netdata

##### Additional Information

issue_context.title: Modular eBPF plugin
issue_context.body:
##### Feature idea summary
The current eBPF plugin is monolithic and we need to change it for we load more eBPF programs. To reach this goal we will follow the same pattern already adopted with `proc.plugin`, in this work the following steps will be done:

- Everything related to the current eBPF program inside `ebpf.c` will be moved to another source file (ebpf_process.c). This implies to move the chart creation function, functions used to read data from kernel ring to user ring and process the data, functions that send messages to Netdata. 
- We will have the following changes in the configuration files: 
- `ebpf.conf` will be the global configurator, but we will create configurations for specific eBPF programs, these files will be created inside `ebpf.d`. 
   -   Create a new section inside that will be used to define the ebpf programs that will be loaded ( `[ebpf programs]` ).
    -  The configurations defined inside the global section of `ebpf.conf` can be overwritten for the specific configurations inside `ebpf.d`.
   - Example:
```
[global]
   load = entry
[ebpf programs]
   process = yes
   network viewer = yes
```

-  Like `proc.plugin` we will also have a global structure that will have the functions to be called in each new file added.
- The ebpf programs can be loaded either using `ebpf.conf` or trough command line arguments.
- Right now we have 3 threads inside the `eBPF plugin` ( "Publisher", "Collector", Log ). We will have only one thread per eBPF program and we group the "Publisher" and "Collector" will be merged inside an unique thread.

##### Expected behavior
Organize the collector to bring new eBPF programs.
comments: One thing I would like is to also organize/structure data a bit better in the plugin itself instead of one big array with all the values.

> One thing I would like is to also organize/structure data a bit better in the plugin itself instead of one big array with all the values.

I agree, I began to work on this in the PR #8879 where I am creating the basis for this PR. You can see there an array of structures that will be passed as arguments for the threads, be free to give any suggestion.

review_comments: We seem to be dragging this problem with fixed indexes around since beginning. Can we do something to fix this once for all? Use hashmap instead of array to store data etc. (so the elements will be named)? I think if we just use some magic values it will bite us in the future as the eBPF functionality is gradualy expanded.
All right, I agree that this is good idea, but can I do this in another PR? And we concentrate effort here to separate the programs.
OK I agree, we can do separate PR that cleans things up and organizes. Best would even be shared HDR for kernel side too. I will resolve this comment then.
I created the issue #9204 for I bring this in a near future.
What if `input` is NULL? Shouldn't we check it here? The same question for `ebpf_process.c`.
The input is allocated with `callocz`, so case we cannot allocate it Netdata will shutdown the collector.
Ok, but `input = input->next`. How you guarantee that you have allocated the same amount of elements as in `move` and put them in a linked list correctly?

`input` and `publish` must be allocated with the same size always,.
I would not like to add this check here, because we will have a check every time that you need to send message to Netdata. I will bring a change that will ensure that when allocated both variables have the same size.
Another point that I would like to call attention, it is for the fact that these functions, like the function that does the allocation of the vectors are `static` inside each collector.
